A.q: Used to describes repeated past actions, habits, and situations. It is followed by which verb form?
options: Base form of the verb
Past simple form
Present continuous form
Third person singular form
A.explain: Used to is followed by the base form of the verb. It describes repeated past actions, habits, and situations. Past simple, continuous, and third person singular are not the form after used to.

A.q: Which sentence correctly describes a repeated past action that no longer happens?
options: My grandmother used to wash clothes by hand
My grandmother used to washed clothes by hand
My grandmother used to washing clothes by hand
My grandmother used to washes clothes by hand
A.explain: Used to + base verb describes repeated past actions. Wash is the base verb. Washed, washing and washes are wrong forms after used to.

A.q: Which sentence correctly describes a past state that is no longer true?
options: Air travel used to be very expensive
Air travel used to was very expensive
Air travel used to being very expensive
Air travel used to is very expensive
A.explain: Used to + base verb describes past states. Be is the base verb. Was, being and is are wrong forms after used to.

A.q: Which form is used instead of used to for single events?
options: Simple past form
Used to form
Present continuous form
Future form
A.explain: Single events use the simple past form. Used to is for repeated actions or past states that are no longer true. Present continuous and future are not past forms.

A.q: The negative form of used to is which structure?
options: Didn't use to + base form
Didn't used to + base form
Don't use to + base form
Won't use to + base form
A.explain: Negative: didn't use to (without -ed) + base form. Didn't used to, don't use to, and won't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Yes/No questions with used to begin with which word?
options: Did
Do
Does
Will
A.explain: Yes/No questions: Did + subject + use to + base form. Short answers use did or didn't. Do, does, and will are not the question form.

A.q: Which correction is needed for 'I use to play'?
options: I used to play
I use to played
I used to played
I use to playing
A.explain: Affirmative used to is spelled with -ed: I used to play. Use to, used to played and use to playing are incorrect forms.

A.q: Which correction is needed for 'How did you used to heat your home'?
options: How did you use to heat your home
How did you used to heated your home
How do you used to heat your home
How did you use to heated your home
A.explain: Questions with did use use to without -ed: How did you use to heat your home. Used to, do you used to and use to heated are incorrect.

A.q: Which sentence correctly describes a past habit that no longer happens?
options: Women used to wear long dresses in the past
Women used to wore long dresses in the past
Women used to wearing long dresses in the past
Women used to wears long dresses in the past
A.explain: Women used to wear long dresses in the past describes a repeated past action. The base form follows used to.

A.q: Which sentence correctly uses simple past for a single event?
options: The nurse checked the patient's blood pressure yesterday
The nurse used to check the patient's blood pressure yesterday
The nurse used to checked the patient's blood pressure yesterday
The nurse used to checking the patient's blood pressure yesterday
A.explain: The event happened once, so simple past is used: checked. Used to is not for single events. Used to checked and used to checking are wrong forms.

A.q: Which is the correct negative?
options: I didn't use to watch TV
I didn't used to watch TV
I don't use to watch TV
I didn't use to watched TV
A.explain: Negative is didn't use to (no -ed) + base form. Didn't used to, don't use to, and past form after use to are incorrect.

A.q: Which is a correct yes/no question?
options: Did you use to watch TV
Did you used to watch TV
Do you use to watch TV
Did you use to watched TV
A.explain: Yes/No questions: Did + subject + use to + base form. Used to, do, and past form are incorrect in the question.

A.q: In the early 1900s, factory workers ___ long hours.
options: used to work
uses to work
was worked
used to worked
A.explain: Used to work describes a repeated past action. Uses to work, was worked and used to worked are incorrect forms after used to.

A.q: Two engineers ___ a new app in 2018.
options: designed
design
used to design
used to designed
A.explain: The action happened once, so simple past is used: designed. Used to is not for single events. Used to designed is a wrong form.

A.q: When we worked on the space station, we ___ the Earth from the observation window.
options: used to watch
use to watch
was watching
used to watched
A.explain: Used to watch describes a repeated past habit. Use to watch, was watching and used to watched are incorrect forms.

A.q: Which correction fixes the missing subject: 'Before invented electricity, people used candles'?
options: Before they invented electricity, people used candles
Before invent electricity, people used candles
Before invented electricity, people used to candles
Before they invent electricity, people used candles
A.explain: Time clauses need a subject: Before they invented electricity. Invent, used to candles and they invent are incorrect forms.

A.q: Which affirmative form is correct?
options: I used to swim
I use to swim
I used to swimming
I was used to swim
A.explain: Affirmative is used to + base verb. Use to, used to swimming and was used to swim are incorrect.

A.q: Which negative form is correct?
options: I didn't use to swim
I didn't used to swim
I don't use to swim
I wasn't use to swim
A.explain: Negative is didn't use to + base verb. Didn't used to, don't use to, and wasn't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Which question form is correct?
options: Did you use to swim?
Did you used to swim?
Do you use to swim?
Were you use to swim?
A.explain: Questions use Did + subject + use to + base verb. Did used to, Do you use to and Were you use to are incorrect.

A.q: Rewrite: Last month I took the bus to work. Now I don't.
options: I used to take the bus to work
I use to take the bus to work
I used to taking the bus to work
I was used to take the bus to work
A.explain: A past habit that stopped uses used to + base form. The other options contain form errors.

A.q: Rewrite: Ten years ago I lived near the hospital. Now I don't.
options: I used to live near the hospital
I use to live near the hospital
I used to living near the hospital
I was used to live near the hospital
A.explain: A past habit that no longer happens uses used to + base form.

A.q: Rewrite: Before I didn't wear a watch. Now I do.
options: I didn't use to wear a watch
I didn't used to wear a watch
I don't use to wear a watch
I wasn't use to wear a watch
A.explain: The negative form for a past habit that changed is didn't use to + base form.

A.q: Rewrite: Last year my brother didn't read books. Now he reads books.
options: He didn't use to read books
He didn't used to read books
He don't use to read books
He wasn't use to read books
A.explain: Correct form is He didn't use to read books. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Rewrite: A long time ago people didn't have smartphones. Now people have smartphones.
options: People didn't use to have smartphones
People didn't used to have smartphones
People don't use to have smartphones
People wasn't use to have smartphones
A.explain: A past state that no longer exists uses didn't use to + base form.

A.q: Rewrite: When I was young I was afraid of heights. Now I'm not.
options: I used to be afraid of heights
I use to be afraid of heights
I used to was afraid of heights
I was used to be afraid of heights
A.explain: Used to be works for past states. Use to, used to was and was used to be are incorrect.

A.q: Rewrite: A long time ago people didn't have computers. Now people have computers.
options: People didn't use to have computers
People didn't used to have computers
People don't use to have computers
People wasn't use to have computers
A.explain: Correct form is People didn't use to have computers. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Rewrite: When Tom was younger he was thin. Now Tom is strong.
options: Tom used to be thin
Tom use to be thin
Tom used to was thin
Tom was used to be thin
A.explain: Correct rewrite is Tom used to be thin. Use to, used to was and was used to be are incorrect.

A.q: She ___ at the hospital before she retired. Now she is so busy.
options: used to work
uses to work
used to working
use to worked
A.explain: Used to work is the correct past habit. Uses to work is present. Used to working and use to worked are wrong.

A.q: Correct: Before the hospital use to have a single entrance, visitors went through the main gate.
options: Before the hospital used to have a single entrance
Before the hospital use to have a single entrance
Before the hospital used to had a single entrance
Before the hospital use to had a single entrance
A.explain: The affirmative form is used to + base verb. The other options contain spelling or form errors.

A.q: Correct: The hospital use to have only one ambulance for emergencies.
options: The hospital used to have only one ambulance
The hospital use to have only one ambulance
The hospital used to had only one ambulance
The hospital uses to have only one ambulance
A.explain: Correct is used to have. Use to, used to had, and uses to are incorrect.

A.q: Correct: Many nurses didn't used to believe in mental health treatment.
options: Many nurses didn't use to believe
Many nurses didn't used to believe
Many nurses don't use to believe
Many nurses wasn't use to believe
A.explain: Negative is didn't use to. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect forms.

A.q: Correct: Nurses use to write all patient records by hand.
options: Nurses used to write all patient records by hand
Nurses use to write all patient records by hand
Nurses used to wrote all patient records by hand
Nurses uses to write all patient records by hand
A.explain: Correct is used to write. Use to, used to wrote, and uses to are incorrect.

A.q: Correct: My grandmother use to visit the same doctor for more than 20 years.
options: My grandmother used to visit the same doctor
My grandmother use to visit the same doctor
My grandmother used to visited the same doctor
My grandmother uses to visit the same doctor
A.explain: Correct is used to visit. Use to, used to visited, and uses to are incorrect.

A.q: Correct: Before discovered antibiotics, what did people use to do?
options: Before antibiotics were discovered, what did people use to do?
Before antibiotics discovered, what did people use to do?
Before antibiotics were discovered, what did people used to do?
Before antibiotics were discovered, what people use to do?
A.explain: The time clause needs a subject and passive form: Before antibiotics were discovered. Questions also use Did + use to (not used to).

A.q: Correct: Did you used to work night shifts at the clinic?
options: Did you use to work night shifts at the clinic?
Did you used to work night shifts at the clinic?
Did you use to worked night shifts at the clinic?
Do you use to work night shifts at the clinic?
A.explain: Yes/No questions use Did + subject + use to + base form.

A.q: Which sentence correctly shows a stopped past habit?
options: I used to play tennis
I use to play tennis
I used to playing tennis
I was used to play tennis
A.explain: Used to + base verb shows a past habit that stopped. Use to, used to playing and was used to play are incorrect.

A.q: Which negative used-to form is correct for a changed habit?
options: I didn't use to drink coffee
I didn't used to drink coffee
I don't use to drink coffee
I wasn't use to drink coffee
A.explain: Didn't use to is the correct negative. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Which past-state form with be is correct?
options: I used to be afraid of the dark
I use to be afraid of the dark
I used to was afraid of the dark
I was used to be afraid of the dark
A.explain: Used to be is correct for past states. Use to, used to was and was used to be are incorrect.

A.q: Which error-correction item needs used to?
options: Nurses used to write all patient records by hand
Nurses use to write all patient records by hand
Nurses used to wrote all patient records by hand
Nurses uses to write all patient records by hand
A.explain: Correct form is used to write. Use to, used to wrote, and uses to are incorrect.

A.q: Which used-to question form is correct?
options: Did she use to teach at the school?
Did she used to teach at the school?
Did she use to taught at the school?
Do she use to teach at the school?
A.explain: Did + use to + base verb is correct. Did used to, did use to taught and Do she use to are incorrect.

A.q: Which rewrite shows a past state that changed?
options: Sarah used to be short
Sarah use to be short
Sarah used to was short
Sarah was used to be short
A.explain: Used to be is correct for past states. Use to, used to was, and was used to be are incorrect.

A.q: Which form correctly uses didn't use to?
options: Many doctors didn't use to prescribe antibiotics
Many doctors didn't used to prescribe antibiotics
Many doctors don't use to prescribe antibiotics
Many doctors wasn't use to prescribe antibiotics
A.explain: Negative is didn't use to. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect forms.

A.q: Which sentence is correct for a past habit?
options: He used to work in a factory when he was young
He uses to work in a factory when he was young
He used to working in a factory when he was young
He use to worked in a factory when he was young
A.explain: Used to work is correct. Uses to work, used to working and use to worked are incorrect forms.

A.q: Which rewrite correctly uses didn't use to?
options: People didn't use to travel by plane
People didn't used to travel by plane
People don't use to travel by plane
People wasn't use to travel by plane
A.explain: Didn't use to is correct. Didn't used to, don't use to and wasn't use to are incorrect.

A.q: Which affirmative used-to form is correct for a past habit?
options: I used to watch cartoons on Saturday
I use to watch cartoons on Saturday
I used to watching cartoons on Saturday
I was used to watch cartoons on Saturday
A.explain: Used to + base verb is correct. Use to, used to watching and was used to watch are incorrect.

A.q: Did you use to swim? Yes, I ___.
options: did
do
used to
use to
A.explain: Short answers with used-to questions use did or didn't. The correct short answer is: Yes, I did.

A.q: Did they use to live here? No, they ___.
options: didn't
don't
used not
use not
A.explain: The negative short answer is: No, they didn't. Don't is present tense, and used not/use not are not short answers.

A.q: Which question is correct?
options: What did you use to watch?
What you used to watch?
What did you used to watch?
What do you use to watch?
A.explain: Object questions use: Wh-word + did + subject + use to + base verb. The correct form is: What did you use to watch?

A.q: Which question asks about the subject?
options: Who used to watch Japanese films?
Who did use to watch Japanese films?
Who used to watched Japanese films?
Who use to watch Japanese films?
A.explain: When who is the subject, we do not use did. The correct form is: Who used to watch Japanese films?

A.q: Which is a formal negative form of 'She used to think that'?
options: She used not to think that.
She used to not thinking that.
She use not to think that.
She used not to thought that.
A.explain: A formal negative form is used not to + base verb: She used not to think that. The common negative is: She didn't use to think that.

A.q: Rewrite: Before we had the internet, we went to the library a lot.
options: Before we had the internet, we used to go to the library a lot.
Before we had the internet, we use to go to the library a lot.
Before we had the internet, we used to went to the library a lot.
Before we had the internet, we used to going to the library a lot.
A.explain: The past habitual action can be rewritten with used to + base verb: we used to go. The time clause remains in simple past: Before we had the internet.

A.q: Which correction fixes the missing subject: 'When finally found the cure, the scientist received an award'?
options: When he finally found the cure, the scientist received an award.
When finally found the cure, the scientist received an award.
When he finally find the cure, the scientist received an award.
When finally he found the cure, the scientist received an award.
A.explain: Time clauses need a subject. The corrected sentence is: When he finally found the cure, the scientist received an award.

A.q: Did the pharmacist use to prepare the mixtures in the old lab? Yes, he ___.
options: did
do
used to
use to
A.explain: Short answers to Did + subject + use to questions use did or didn't. The correct short answer is: Yes, he did.

A.q: Did the students use to memorize every drug name? No, they ___.
options: didn't
don't
used not
use not
A.explain: The negative short answer is didn't. Don't is present tense, and used not / use not are not short answers.

A.q: Which question correctly asks about the thing people did in the past?
options: What did patients use to take for fever?
What patients used to take for fever?
What did patients used to take for fever?
What do patients use to take for fever?
A.explain: Object questions with used to use: Wh-word + did + subject + use to + base verb. The correct form is: What did patients use to take for fever?

A.q: Which question correctly asks about the person who had the past habit?
options: Who used to check the ward before rounds?
Who did use to check the ward before rounds?
Who used to checked the ward before rounds?
Who use to check the ward before rounds?
A.explain: When who is the subject, we do not use did. The correct form is: Who used to check the ward before rounds?

A.q: Which sentence uses the formal negative pattern with used to?
options: The consultant used not to answer calls after midnight.
The consultant used to not answered calls after midnight.
The consultant use not to answer calls after midnight.
The consultant used not to answering calls after midnight.
A.explain: A formal negative form is used not to + base verb: The consultant used not to answer calls after midnight. The common negative is: The consultant didn't use to answer calls after midnight.

A.q: Complete: Before hospitals adopted electronic charts, nurses ___ patient notes by hand.
options: used to write
use to write
used to wrote
used to writing
A.explain: The time clause is in simple past: Before hospitals adopted electronic charts. The main clause uses used to + base verb: nurses used to write.

A.q: Which correction fixes the missing subject in: When completed the training, they updated the safety log?
options: When the technicians completed the training, they updated the safety log.
When completed the training, they updated the safety log.
When the technicians complete the training, they updated the safety log.
When completed the technicians training, they updated the safety log.
A.explain: Time clauses need an explicit subject. The corrected sentence is: When the technicians completed the training, they updated the safety log.

A.q: My brother ___ when he was younger, but now he runs every morning.
options: didn't use to exercise
didn't used to exercise
don't use to exercise
didn't use to exercising
A.explain: The negative form is didn't use to + base verb. Didn't used to, don't use to, and didn't use to exercising are incorrect.

A.q: Which pair correctly shows a repeated past habit, with the second form emphasizing it is no longer true?
options: In the 1990s, nurses filed reports manually. / In the 1990s, nurses used to file reports manually.
In the 1990s, nurses filed reports manually. / In the 1990s, nurses used to filed reports manually.
In the 1990s, nurses use to file reports manually. / In the 1990s, nurses filed reports manually.
In the 1990s, nurses used to filing reports manually. / In the 1990s, nurses file reports manually.
A.explain: Simple past can describe a repeated past action. Used to + base verb emphasizes the habit is finished. Used to filed, use to file and used to filing are wrong forms.

A.q: ___ he ___ play tennis when he was young?
options: Did / use to
Does / use to
Was / use to
Did / used to
A.explain: Used-to questions use Did + subject + use to + base verb. The correct form is Did he use to play tennis?

A.q: Did he use to play tennis when he was young? Yes, ___.
options: he did
he used to
he does
he was
A.explain: Short answers to Did...? questions use did or didn't. The correct short answer is Yes, he did.

A.q: What ___ you ___ watch as a child?
options: did / use to
do / use to
did / used to
are / using to
A.explain: Object Wh-questions with used to use: Wh-word + did + subject + use to + base verb. The correct form is What did you use to watch?

A.q: Who ___ Japanese films as a child?
options: used to watch
use to watch
did use to watch
used to watched
A.explain: When who is the subject, we do not use did. The correct form is Who used to watch Japanese films?

A.q: She ___ the answer when she was younger, but now she does not.
options: used to know
use to know
used to knew
was knowing
A.explain: Used to can be followed by a stative verb in the base form. The correct sentence is She used to know the answer.

A.q: In old times, people ___ to the radio for news.
options: used to listen
use to listen
used to listened
were listen
A.explain: A repeated past habit uses used to + base verb. The correct form is people used to listen to the radio.

A.q: There ___ many students in the class in the past, but now there are few.
options: used to be
use to be
used to been
was used to be
A.explain: The structure for a past state that no longer exists is There used to be + noun. The correct form is There used to be many students.

A.q: What ___ people ___ do before television existed?
options: did / use to
do / use to
did / used to
are / using to
A.explain: Wh-questions with used to use: Wh-word + did + subject + use to + base verb. The correct form is What did people use to do?

A.q: Which sentence correctly describes a past situation that no longer exists?
options: There used to be a small clinic on this street
There use to be a small clinic on this street
There used to was a small clinic on this street
There was used to be a small clinic on this street
A.explain: There used to be + noun describes a past situation that no longer exists.
